chapter.intro: Intro: The Man With Many Faces
intro.title: The Man With Many Faces
intro.1: Three days from now, in Ironhaven, the city of iron and snow.
intro.2: A man who has been many people wakes in a cell, with nobody's face but his own.
line.i.plateLook: A dented tin plate. Still shiny where the dent is.
line.i.crustLook: Yesterday's bread. Today it's a brick. Tomorrow it could be a face.
line.i.nailLook: A nail from the cot, bent. A poor key, but not a hopeless one.
line.i.stripLook: A strip torn from the blanket. Long enough to reach a table.
line.i.hookLineLook: The nail tied to the strip. A fishing line for a very small pond.
line.i.frameLook: Nessa's frame. Brass ribs, little hinges at the jaw. Wear it under a face and the face moves when I talk.
line.i.plasterLook: Flakes of damp plaster. Dry, they crumble. Wet, they set.
line.i.wetPlasterLook: Plaster gone soft in bucket water. It wants something to hold it together.
line.i.puttyLook: Plaster kneaded into bread. It holds a shape. It even smells a little like a sergeant.
line.i.maskHarrowLook: Sergeant Harrow's heavy jaw and pouched eyes, with a little of my own hair for his eyebrows. In candlelight, he'd fool his mother.
line.i.keysLook: Benn's key ring. He won't miss it until he needs it.
line.i.hoodLook: A clerk's hood, ink on the cuffs. Nobody looks under a clerk's hood.
line.i.ledgerLook: The tally ledger. A clerk carrying a ledger is invisible.
line.i.maskClerkLook: Hood and ledger. Not a mask, a posture: shoulders down, eyes on the numbers.
line.i.heroLook: Silas. Thin, clever, and currently a prisoner. Two of those can change.
line.i.heroLookHarrow: Sergeant Harrow, as far as anyone in this light can tell.
line.i.heroLookClerk: A tally clerk. Grey, harmless, forgettable. Perfect.
line.i.heroTalk: Talking to myself again. At least the company is good.
line.i.maskHarrowOn: I settle the frame and press Harrow's face onto it. The jaw moves when mine does. Hello, Sergeant.
line.i.maskClerkOn: Hood up, ledger under my arm, shoulders down. Nobody worth a second look.
line.i.harrowCracked: Harrow's face cracked as it dried. It served its turn.
line.i.wake1: Damp stone. A cold that gets into the teeth. And no face but my own.
line.i.wake2: One candle, out past the bars. Somebody snoring next to it.
line.i.plateTake: A tin plate, and a crust on it. Supper, apparently.
line.i.windowLook: A barred window, high up. A thread of moonlight comes in and dies on the floor.
line.i.windowLookLit: The moon, borrowed and put to work.
line.i.windowUse: Too high and too small. Even for me.
line.i.angle1: I catch the moonlight in the dent of the plate and tilt it...
line.i.angle2: There. The whole cell, silver and dripping.
line.i.angle3: A cot, a bucket, a wall that weeps. And out there, on the guard's table: my frame.
line.i.alreadyLit: The light's where I want it.
line.i.cotLook: Straw and a blanket that has given up.
line.i.cotDark: I can't see what I'd be grabbing.
line.i.nailTake: One of the cot's nails was already loose. Now it's bent, and mine.
line.i.stripTake: I tear a long strip from the blanket. It wasn't keeping anyone warm anyway.
line.i.cotEmpty: I've taken everything that comes off it.
line.i.wallLook: The wall weeps. The plaster comes away in wet, grey flakes.
line.i.plasterTake: A handful of plaster. A sculptor has worked with worse.
line.i.wallEnough: I have enough of the wall.
line.i.bucketLook: A bucket of water. I've decided to believe it's water.
line.i.wetPlaster: I soak the plaster. It goes soft and grey and willing.
line.i.soggyBread: Soggy bread is still bread. It needs something to mix with first.
line.i.putty: Plaster kneaded into bread. A putty that holds a shape.
line.i.needFace: The putty is ready. Whose face, though? I need someone to copy.
line.i.plasterDry: Dry plaster won't take a shape. It needs water, and something to bind it.
line.i.harrowMade1: Brow, jaw, the heavy pouches under the eyes. A pinch of my own hair for his eyebrows.
line.i.harrowMade2: Sergeant Harrow, on Nessa's frame. Not my best work, but it moves when I speak.
line.i.candleLook: A stub of candle on the guard's table. The only warm thing down here.
line.i.candleTake: It's on the far side of the bars.
line.i.tableLookDark: A table by the candle. Something on it glints.
line.i.tableLook: The guard's table: the candle, a cup, and my mask frame, confiscated. Just out of reach.
line.i.tableLookEmpty: The candle and a cup. The interesting thing is in my satchel now.
line.i.outOfReach: Out of reach. My arms are long, but not that long.
line.i.frameReach: An arm's length and a bit beyond the bars. I need a longer arm.
line.i.fishDark: I can't fish for what I can't see.
line.i.fish1: Through the bars, slowly. Don't wake him.
line.i.fish2: The nail catches a brass rib...
line.i.fish3: Got it. Nessa's frame, back where it belongs. The strip stays snagged on the table; the nail I keep.
line.i.roster1: The duty roster. Nights: Benn, cells. Kell, guardroom. Sergeant Harrow, in charge.
line.i.roster2: And someone has sketched Harrow in the margin: heavy jaw, pouched eyes, a moustache like a broom. A face to copy.
line.i.rosterAgain: Harrow: jaw, pouches, broom moustache. I have him.
line.i.cellDoorLook: The cell door. A good lock on a bad hinge.
line.i.notWatched: Not while he's sitting right there.
line.i.pick1: Bent nail in the lock. Feel for the pins... one... two...
line.i.doorOpen: The door swings open. Quietly, for once.
line.i.stairsLook: Stairs up, past the guard's chair.
line.i.barsFirst: The bars are in the way.
line.i.readDark: I can barely see him. I can hear him, though.
line.i.readGuard1: He's apologising in his sleep. Cold, tired, and more afraid of his sergeant than of any prisoner.
line.i.readGuard2: A man like that does what his sergeant says. Especially when it lets him get warm.
line.i.readGuardAgain: Cold, tired, afraid of Harrow. Everything I need.
line.i.guardLookDark: A shape in a chair by the candle. Snoring.
line.i.guardLook: A young guard, shivering, asleep with his chin on his chest. A key ring at his belt.
line.i.shout3: He'd sleep through a war. He won't wake for me. Maybe for someone else.
line.i.noShout: Shouting as myself gets me nowhere.
line.i.guardItem: He's asleep. And on the far side of the bars.
line.i.afterGuard: Gone up to the stove. The mask cracked as he went. Now, the lock.
line.i.afterGuardKeys: Gone, and his keys stayed with me. Harrow's face cracked as he went. Never mind.
line.i.caught.guard: Hang on. Harrow's in Coppersong. Who's... GUARDS!
line.i.caught.think.guard: That's how it would go, if I played it like that. Again. Slower. Remember what I read in him.
line.i.caught.think.warden: No. That's how it ends badly. Think it through again: what does Kell want?
line.i.warden1: A guardroom, warm from the stove. And a guard who is very much awake.
line.i.warden2: He'll know the real Harrow. That face won't survive a second look up here.
line.i.hoodTake: The clerk's hood. It smells of ink and resignation.
line.i.ledgerLook1: Columns of numbers: bread, coal, candles, prisoners.
line.i.ledgerLook2: And in the back, a page of debts. Kell owes the quartermaster for dice.
line.i.ledgerTake: I take the ledger. A man with a ledger is a man with a reason to be anywhere.
line.i.clerkMade: Hood and ledger. Not a mask: a posture. Shoulders down, eyes on the numbers.
line.i.stoveLook: The stove. Benn will be very happy next to it, wherever he's got to.
line.i.grateLook: An iron grate, and the night beyond it. The lock is old.
line.i.keysWrong: None of Benn's keys fit. The grate's on Harrow's ring.
line.i.grateOpen: The grate swings open onto the snow.
line.i.readWarden1: Kell. Awake, but not by choice: he keeps looking at the clock, and at the kitchen door.
line.i.readWarden2: Hungry. Bored. And he flinches whenever anyone mentions the quartermaster.
line.i.readWarden3: A man in debt to the quartermaster doesn't argue with the quartermaster's clerk.
line.i.readWardenAgain: Hungry, bored, in debt. Three handles.
line.i.wardenLook: Broad, awake, and the type who'd know his own sergeant's face anywhere.
line.i.wardenLookBusy: Kell's in the kitchen doorway, chewing.
line.i.notHarrowHere: Not with Harrow's face. Kell knows the real one too well.
line.i.notAsMyself: As myself? He'd have me back in the cell before I finished a sentence.
line.i.afterWarden: Off to the kitchen. Now the grate.
line.i.wallsLook: Ironhaven's walls, black against the snow.
line.i.sigridLook: An officer in a long coat, waiting. As if she knew I'd come out this door.
line.i.readSigrid: Nothing. She gives away nothing. That's new.
dlgI.guard.wake1: Wha-? Sergeant Harrow! I wasn't sleeping, sir!
dlgI.guard.wake2: Sir, you're... in the cell, sir?
dlgI.choice.asleep: Inspecting the cell you were meant to be watching, Benn. Asleep. Again.
dlgI.guard.keysAsk: My keys, sir? But you've got your own ring...
dlgI.guard.friend: Friend, sir? Are you feeling all right, Sergeant?
dlgI.guard.scolded1: Sorry, Sergeant. It's the cold, sir. It gets into your bones down here.
dlgI.guard.scolded2: It won't happen again, sir. I swear.
dlgI.choice.warm: You're no use to me frozen. Go up and warm yourself at the stove. I'll watch him.
dlgI.guard.report: Report, sir? Nothing to report, sir. You'd know, sir. You're in there.
dlgI.guard.prisoner: The prisoner? He's... wasn't he... where is he, sir?
dlgI.guard.warm1: Really, sir? Thank you, sir! You're a good man, Sergeant, whatever they say.
dlgI.guard.warm2: Let me salute you proper, sir.
dlgI.choice.palm: Clap his shoulder through the bars, and lift the key ring.
dlgI.choice.tally: Tally clerk. Quartermaster wants the night count. Your name's in his book, Kell.
dlgI.warden.passing: Nobody passes through here. Not at this hour.
dlgI.warden.orders: Harrow didn't say anything to me. And I know all Harrow's errand-boys.
dlgI.warden.tally1: The quartermaster? At this hour? ...What's he say about me?
dlgI.warden.tally2: Look, I'll pay him. Tell him I'll pay him.
dlgI.choice.kitchen: I'll count slowly. Long enough for a man to fetch his supper, say.
dlgI.choice.grate: Open the grate for me, would you?
dlgI.warden.grate: Open the grate? Why would a clerk need the grate?
dlgI.sigrid.1: The tally clerk doesn't come at night. And he's a head shorter than you.
dlgI.sigrid.2: Benn's upstairs, toasting his feet. He says Sergeant Harrow sent him. Harrow has been in Coppersong for a week.
dlgI.choice.clerk: Would you believe I'm a very tall clerk?
dlgI.sigrid.leaving: You were. Then you met me.
dlgI.sigrid.frame1: That frame under your hood. Brass, articulated. Who made it?
dlgI.sigrid.frame3: Out of bread, plaster and the wall of your own cell, you made a sergeant. I have a use for a man who can be anyone.
dlgI.sigrid.frame4: Walk with me. Before the real Harrow comes back from Coppersong.
hint.i.light.1: The moonlight from the window is thin. Something shiny could throw it further.
hint.i.light.2: Take the tin plate and use it on the window.
hint.i.frame.1: The frame lies on the guard's table, beyond reach. The cot might give a longer arm.
hint.i.frame.2: Take the nail and a strip from the cot, tie them together, and use the hook line on the table.
obj.i.face: Make a face the guard will obey.
hint.i.face.1: Who is the guard afraid of? The roster on the wall shows a face. The wall and the bucket give material.
hint.i.face.2: Look at the roster. Take plaster, wet it in the bucket, knead it with the crust, then use the putty on the frame.
hint.i.guard.1: Wear the mask and speak to him. What did you read in him?
hint.i.guard.2: Read the guard first. Then, as Harrow, scold him and send him up to get warm.
hint.i.door.1: Keys, or something to pick the lock with.
hint.i.door.2: Use the key ring or the bent nail on the cell door.
hint.i.past.1: Kell knows Harrow. Someone else, then: there's a hood and a ledger here.
hint.i.past.2: Read Kell, take the hood and the ledger, put them together, wear the guise, and talk to him.
hint.i.grate.2: Once Kell is busy, use the bent nail on the grate.
note.i.guard: Benn: cold, tired, afraid of Sergeant Harrow.
note.i.harrow: Harrow: heavy jaw, pouched eyes, broom moustache.
note.i.warden: Kell: hungry, bored, owes the quartermaster for dice.
diary.intro.cell: Woke in Ironhaven's cells with nothing but my own face, which has never been much use to me.
diary.intro.frame: Fished Nessa's frame off the guard's table with a nail and a strip of blanket. With the frame, I can be anyone.
diary.intro.harrow: Made Sergeant Harrow out of bread and plaster. His own guard saluted him.
diary.intro.clerk: Upstairs, a guard who knew Harrow too well. So I became nobody: a clerk with a ledger.
diary.intro.sigrid: Captain Sigrid was waiting at the door. She saw through me at once, and then offered me work.
end.intro.text: Silas walks out of Ironhaven beside the captain who caught him. That is three days from now. The story starts where the cold does: in Cinderfold.
line.i.hookLine: I tie the nail to the end of the strip. A fishing line for a very small pond.
